text: The system shall accept the declaration of an act on the outside world, a change to a declared act and the removal of a declared act.
rationale: REQ-PL-031 gives each declaration a new, a change and a removal, and the property is that the path is whole. The first text stated the three in three rows.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of an act that does not state the external service that the act reaches and the form of its arguments.
rationale: DEC-103. The external service is where External Access carries the call, and the form of the arguments is what a caller supplies and what Authorization judges (FUN-AU-02). Nothing else is declared: whether an act needs authorization is judged over the act with its arguments, and whether it is hard to reverse is not stated.

text: The system shall refuse the removal of a declared act that a position names.
rationale: DEC-071 refuses a removal that another declaration depends on. A position that names a removed act admits nothing where it stated an act, and nothing says so. REQ-ST-050, REQ-IN-027 and REQ-WC-045 state the same refusal, and REQ-AD-053 supplies whether a position names a declaration.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of an act, a change to an act and the removal of an act from an agent only.
rationale: REQ-PL-028 and DEC-053. To structure a statement of the user into a declaration is a judgement that DEC-030 keeps out of the platform. The three name one writer, as REQ-AU-002 states for a class.

text: The system shall hold, with each declared act, the writer that declared it and the time of the declaration.
rationale: REQ-PL-029 and DEC-061. REQ-AU-011 and REQ-ST-031 hold the writer with each declared class and kind for the same reason: a reader must see which agent declared an act. The first text held the writer only, and REQ-PL-029 states the time as well.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of an act, a change to an act and the removal of an act from a caller whose position does not admit it.
rationale: DEC-019 and DEC-029. REQ-AU-012, REQ-ST-032 and REQ-WC-023 state the same refusal at the other declaration boundaries.

text: The system shall refuse a call to an act on the outside world unless it confirms that the position of the caller admits that act.
rationale: REQ-PL-005 keeps an agent inside the authority that its position gives, and DEC-019 makes each boundary refuse. This system holds the acts on the outside world, so it is their boundary. A caller can call an act that it was not shown, so REQ-AC-008 does not refuse (DEC-102). A position that cannot be confirmed is refused, as REQ-WC-030 states for a unit of work.

text: The system shall give a caller each act that the position of the caller admits, with the form of the arguments of that act.
rationale: DEC-069 and DEC-102. REQ-AD-052 states in the rules where a caller finds the acts, and this is where it finds them. A caller reads an act when it needs it, so a change to an act reaches every caller at once and no copy goes stale.

text: The system shall give the acts, and accept a call to an act, through an interface that a client that another person wrote can use without a change to that client.
rationale: REQ-PL-011 makes the interface sufficient for a client that another person wrote to operate an agent, and DEC-087 attaches that client to an agent through Interaction (REQ-IA-005). The agent then calls the acts from that client, so this interface must be one that such a client already uses. Which interface is below this level. OPN-061.

text: The system shall carry each call to an act that another system holds to that system.
rationale: DEC-102. The system that holds the act refuses and does it, so this system carries the call and makes no judgement (DEC-030). The first text also carried a released gated unit, which is a second item from a second function and is REQ-AC-026.

text: The system shall give a caller the result of each act that it called, as the system that did the act gives it.
rationale: A caller needs the result to continue. The result of a read of State Custody carries the writer, the source and the times (REQ-ST-014), and the result of a read of the declared classes is the statement of Authorization (REQ-AU-006, REQ-AU-009), so this system gives each one as it receives it and holds no copy. A gated act returns its result through Work and Coordination (REQ-AC-020), because the caller does not hold it (DEC-066).

text: The system shall refuse a call to an act on the outside world that is not declared.
rationale: REQ-PL-014 makes no action on the outside world reachable by a path that does not use REQ-PL-012. An act that is not declared has no stated form, so Authorization cannot judge it and the record cannot state it.

text: The system shall give Authorization each act on the outside world that a caller calls, with its arguments, for classification.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 makes the platform tell the difference between an action that needs authorization and one that does not. DEC-103 has Authorization judge the act with its arguments, because REQ-PL-013 gates a message to a third party and not a message to the user. DEC-102 classifies each act on the outside world at the call, and the holder of an act inside the platform gates it.

text: The system shall accept from Authorization whether an act that a caller called is in a declared class.
rationale: REQ-AU-004 supplies the answer. REQ-AU-008 answers that an act is in a declared class when Authorization cannot decide.

text: The system shall treat an act on the outside world as in a declared class when Authorization gives no answer to its classification within TBD.
rationale: DEC-110 and OPN-051. To continue is the effect of RSK-AU-001, and to stop makes RSK-AU-006 total, so the user becomes the fallback for an act on the outside world. The value depends on REQ-AU-010 and is TBD (rule 13). DEC-102 classifies only an act on the outside world.

text: The system shall refuse a call to an act on the outside world that is in a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 and DEC-104. A call carries no answer of the user, so an act in a declared class is done only when Work and Coordination sends it released with its answer. REQ-AC-018 then checks that the request states the act that is done. The first text also told the caller why, which is REQ-AC-029.

text: The system shall accept from Work and Coordination each released gated unit, with the affirmative answer to it.
rationale: REQ-WC-069 and REQ-WC-058 send it, and DEC-108 sends every released gated unit here, whichever system holds its act. OPN-079.

text: The system shall not do or carry a released gated unit unless the affirmative answer that it receives with it is to a request that states its act with its arguments.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 refuses an action until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that action. REQ-WC-068 checks this before it sends, and this row checks it where the act is done or handed to its holder, for every gated act (DEC-108, OPN-083). DEC-105 makes the arguments state the effect, so the answer binds to what occurs. The first text named an act in a declared class. This system does not classify an act inside the platform, so the row covers every released gated unit.

text: The system shall give each act on the outside world that it admits to External Access as a call to the external service that the declaration of the act states.
rationale: DEC-032 makes External Access the only route to an external service, and DEC-107 makes this system the only one that refuses an act on the outside world. External Access checks no authority, so a call reaches it only after this system admitted and classified the act.

text: The system shall give Work and Coordination the result of each gated act, or that its call returned no result.
rationale: REQ-WC-070 closes a gated unit with the result, and the raiser reads it there (REQ-WC-021). DEC-108 returns every result through this system, so Work and Coordination has one supplier of it. OPN-079. The first text gave the result only. A call that returns no result still ends the gated unit, and REQ-AC-024 does not repeat it, so Work and Coordination must be told.

text: The system shall give Self-Observation, for each act on the outside world that it did, the act with its arguments, the agent that called it or raised its gated unit, the time, the result, and the authority as the unit of work that holds the affirmative answer or as the declared class that states that the act needs no authorization of the user.
rationale: REQ-PL-014 and DEC-106. This system holds no body (DEC-024), so the record is held as data about the platform. DEC-050 keeps the answer with the unit of work that asked, and a copy is a second record of one answer that drifts (DEC-019), so the record names the unit. DEC-109 gates an act on the outside world that no class names, so an act that is done without an answer is one that a declared class exempts, and the record names that class. A gated act is done for its raiser and not at a call. The first text named the classification that the act is in no declared class, and the agent that called the act. The user may remove the record under REQ-PL-026, and DEC-106 accepts that what it held is then lost.

text: The system shall state the agent and the time of each act on the outside world, and shall not accept them from the caller.
rationale: REQ-PL-029 and DEC-056. A caller that states its own identity attributes its act to another agent.

text: The system shall give Self-Observation the record of an act on the outside world before it gives that act to External Access.
rationale: RSK-AC-003. A process can stop between the call and the record, and then the act occurred and nothing states it. A record that exists before the call and has no result shows an act whose result is not known, which a reader can find. REQ-AC-021 states what the record holds. The first text also completed the record, which is REQ-AC-030.

text: The system shall not repeat an act on the outside world whose call returned no result.
rationale: RSK-AC-004. A call that returns no result may have had its effect, because the failure can come after the effect. An error is a result and states that nothing occurred, and no result states nothing. DEC-048 permits the action that the request states and no other, and a repeat is another action. This system holds no body (DEC-024), so it knows which calls have no result from the records of REQ-AC-023. The first text also told the caller, which is REQ-AC-031. A call that the caller makes again is a new call and is classified again: what the caller does with no result is agent behaviour (MET-002). An act that a declared class exempts is not seen by the user again when the caller repeats it, and that residual is agent behaviour and not a failure of this system.

text: The system shall not do or carry a released gated unit that it did or carried before.
rationale: RSK-AC-005. DEC-048 permits one action for one answer. REQ-WC-029 keeps Work and Coordination from sending a unit two times, and rule 8 refuses a mitigation from a sibling, so this system refuses the second one itself. This system holds no body (DEC-024), so it knows which units it did from the records of REQ-AC-023.

text: The system shall carry each released gated unit whose act another system holds to that system, with its raiser, the affirmative answer and the request that it answers.
rationale: DEC-108 sends every released gated unit here, and REQ-AC-018 checks it before it is carried. The holder then does the act, and REQ-AU-003 and REQ-AU-014 read the answer where a class changes. The holder states the raiser as the writer of what the act changes (REQ-AU-011), so the raiser crosses with the unit. The first text did not carry the raiser.

text: The system shall state, with each call that it carries to another system, the caller of that call, and shall not accept the caller from the call.
rationale: REQ-PL-029 and DEC-056. After DEC-102 the call that a holder observes comes from this system, so the holder cannot observe the caller itself (REQ-ST-037). The holder refuses by the position of the caller (DEC-019), so the caller that it reads must be one that the caller did not state.

text: The system shall not do a released gated unit whose act on the outside world the position of its raiser does not admit.
rationale: RSK-AC-002. REQ-AC-007 refuses a call, and a released gated unit is not a call. Without this row an agent raises a gated unit for an act that its position does not admit, and an answer of the user then does the act. DEC-048 states that a yes is not a change to what a position admits. The holder of an act inside the platform refuses by the position of the raiser that REQ-AC-026 carries (DEC-102), so this row covers the acts that this system holds. The first text also covered a unit that it carries.

text: The system shall give the caller, with each refusal of an act that is in a declared class, that the act needs an affirmative answer of the user.
rationale: DEC-104 has the caller raise the request, and the caller must know that the refusal is one that an answer removes and not one that its position causes.

text: The system shall complete the record of each act on the outside world with the result of its call, or with that the call returned no result.
rationale: RSK-AC-003. REQ-AC-023 gives the record before the call. A record that is not completed is how a reader finds an act whose result is not known.

text: The system shall give the caller of an act on the outside world whose call returned no result that the call returned no result.
rationale: The caller gets the fact and not an interpretation of it, so it can find out what occurred before it calls again. An error is a result and reaches the caller through REQ-AC-011.

text: The system shall give its answer to a call within TBD, apart from the time that the system that does the act takes.
rationale: DEC-102 puts this system on the path of every act, as REQ-AU-010 is on the path of each act on the outside world and REQ-AD-015 is for a position. The value depends on the host and on the caller, and is TBD (rule 13).

text: The system shall accept the result of each act that it carried to another system or gave to External Access.
rationale: REQ-AC-011 gives the result to the caller and REQ-AC-020 gives the result of a gated act to Work and Coordination, and neither accepts it.

text: The system shall refuse a change to a declared act, and the removal of a declared act, that a declared class which states that an act needs no authorization names.
rationale: DEC-071 and DEC-109. An exemption was approved for the act as it was declared, and a change to the service or to the arguments would keep that approval for another act. DEC-109 makes an exemption name each act that it covers, so the dependency can be found. The exemption is changed or removed first, with an answer of the user (REQ-AU-003, REQ-AU-014), and the act is then changed and is gated until an exemption covers it again. A class that gates an act does not block a change, because the changed act stays gated. The first text refused a change for every class that names the act.

text: The system shall not do or carry a released gated unit, or repeat a call to an act on the outside world, when it cannot read the records that state whether it did that act before.
rationale: RSK-AC-004 and RSK-AC-005 rest on the records of REQ-AC-023, which Self-Observation holds (DEC-106). A record that cannot be read gives no evidence that the act did not occur, so the system fails closed. The act waits and is not lost: the gated unit stays with Work and Coordination.
